title: Prompt's minCommitRemainingSeconds restarts on every renewal, but the arbiter's commitment clock does not
description: ActiveIntent() takes acceptedAt from the open history entry of the active intent. IntentArbiter.Renew adds a new history entry stamped with the renewal time, and each Claude proposal has a new IntentId. IntentArbiter.ActiveSince, the clock that actually enforces commitment, is not reset on renewal (its own doc comment says so). After any renewal, the prompt reports a commitment window that has already ended. The system prompt then says replacing the intent inside that window is refused, so propose the same playbook. That instruction produces another renewal, which moves the reported window forward again. A Claude strategist on a 20 s cadence, or Refine on a 5 s cadence, with a 35-60 s minCommit is told on every call that it is locked in.
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a scratch program using the real IntentArbiter, PlaybookLibrary and RulesDatabase: activate allied-grizzly-timing (minCommit 45) at t=0, renew at t=30 (arbiter ActiveSince stays 0), build the prompt at t=60. The prompt shows secondsActive=30, minCommitRemainingSeconds=15. A different playbook offered at t=60 is Activated with reason 'switch'. The model is told a switch will be rejected when it would be accepted, and it keeps renewing the old plan indefinitely.
suggested_fix: Compute secondsActive and minCommitRemainingSeconds from arbiter.ActiveSince. Pass it through StrategistContext (the ValidationContext already carries ActiveSince), or make Renew keep the original AcceptedAt. Then add a prompt test covering the renewal case.

title: Prompt says a fallback- or emergency-installed intent is committed, though the arbiter yields it to any primary proposal
description: IntentArbiter treats an intent installed by the Fallback or Emergency role as a placeholder. It returns Activated 'yield' to any Primary proposal, with no commitment or hysteresis. The prompt still shows minCommitRemainingSeconds for such an intent, gives no role, and the system prompt says replacing it inside the window is only accepted on abort or base threat. In the llm arm the selector fallback fills every LLM gap (the first latency window, and any timeout, refusal or parse failure). Claude is then steered to rubber-stamp the selector's playbook instead of choosing its own. This defeats the placeholder rule, which exists so a slow LLM is not locked out by the placeholder that covered its latency.
failure_scenario: Scratch program: arbiter.Offer(selector intent, role Fallback) at t=0; at t=10 the prompt shows minCommitRemainingSeconds=35. A different primary playbook offered at t=10 is Activated with reason 'yield'. The model has been told the opposite, so it proposes the fallback's playbook, and the renewal promotes the fallback's plan to a primary commitment.
suggested_fix: Expose the active role, or a boolean like 'replaceableNow' or 'placeholder', in activeIntent. Set minCommitRemainingSeconds to 0 or null for placeholders, and state the placeholder rule in the system prompt.

title: Cost accounting drops cache-write tokens and bills cache reads at full input price
description: ProposalCost has no cache-creation field, so ModelUsage.CacheCreationTokens is discarded in ClaudeStrategist. The arena then leaves those tokens out of both TokensIn and Usd. CostUsd charges cacheReadTokens at 1.0x input price. Per the pricing docs it should be 0.1x (0.025x on Fable 5.1), and 5-minute cache writes cost 1.25x. Both breakpoints (system prompt, and a match context of about 12k characters) are ephemeral-cached, so every call is either a write or a read of a few thousand tokens. The arena's 'inference cost' column, a proposal metric, is wrong in both directions. BotArenaAgent also only prices Proposal and ShadowProposal records. Calls that fail after spending tokens (refusal, max_tokens at 16000 output, parse or mapping failures) are logged with their cost but never priced, and the code comment acknowledges this.
failure_scenario: Claude Opus 5 at $5/$25. A warm call with 200 uncached input, 4800 cache-read and 500 output tokens: PriceTable.CostUsd returns $0.0375 (measured), against a true $0.0159 (2.4x over). A cold call reports input=200, cacheRead=0, cacheCreation dropped, so it is priced at $0.0135 against a true $0.0438 (3.2x under), and TokensIn misses the 4800 written tokens. A max_tokens failure costing about $0.40 is priced at $0.
suggested_fix: Add CacheCreationTokens to ProposalCost. Carry per-model cache-read and cache-write multipliers in ModelPrice (0.1x reads, 0.025x for fable-5-1, 1.25x 5-minute writes), and price creation tokens. In BotArenaAgent, also sum cost from DecisionRecordKinds.ProposalFailed records.

title: Refine mode cannot lower attackArmyValue because it keeps the active intent's frozen attack condition
description: Refined() copies the active intent's AttackConditions and takes only the proposed parameters. For allied-grizzly-timing and soviet-rhino-rush, the playbook's AttackConditions contain a hard-coded OwnArmyValue >= default (1500 or 1000), and PlaybookIntents.FromPlaybook copies it into the intent. OperationalPlanner.Squads attacks only when `conditions && army >= attackArmyValue`. A refined attackArmyValue below the playbook default therefore has no effect, and the attack still waits for the frozen threshold. The catalogue advertises a range of [800, 3000] (or [600, 2000]), so the Refine model (Haiku) is invited to make a change that silently does nothing.
failure_scenario: Active intent allied-grizzly-timing with the default attack condition OwnArmyValue Ge 1500. The Refine model returns attackArmyValue=900 to hit an early window. Refined keeps AttackConditions [OwnArmyValue>=1500]. With army value 1000, `conditions` is false and no attack is launched, although the accepted intent says 900.
suggested_fix: Rebuild parameter-driven conditions when refining (for example, rewrite OwnArmyValue thresholds from attackArmyValue). Or drop the hard-coded OwnArmyValue attack condition from those playbooks, since the planner already gates on attackArmyValue.

title: Rule facts omit counters and have no rows for observed enemy types, which the proposal requires
description: The proposal requires 'an authoritative rules database for costs, timings, prerequisites and counters. Never ask the LLM to remember those reliably.' ruleFacts.units lists only own-faction units (the cheapest 4 per role), with weapon class but no Armor, Damage or IRulesDatabase.Effectiveness data. Enemy typeIds that appear in features.enemy.knownTech and knownProduction (already observed, so not a fog issue) have no rule row at all. title: Inference cost omits cache-creation tokens and every failed request's tokens
description: ModelUsage carries CacheCreationTokens, but ProposalCost has no field for them and ClaudeStrategist drops them. PriceTable.CostUsd therefore never charges cache writes, even though the prompt builder deliberately caches the system prompt and a stable prefix, so every match's first call writes a large cache. The input-token count excludes them as well. Replies that fail after billing (max_tokens, refusal, parse or mapping failure, refine playbook switch) return null. Their cost reaches only the ProposalFailed record, and BotArenaAgent never sums that record ('Failed requests still cost tokens...').
failure_scenario: A live llm run where each match's first request writes about 3k cached prompt tokens and a few replies hit max_tokens. The report's 'tokens and USD per match' leaves out all cache-write tokens and the output tokens of the truncated replies, so the inference cost is understated.
suggested_fix: Add CacheCreationTokens to ProposalCost (it is a contract change, so record it) and price cache writes. In BotArenaAgent, also sum the cost carried by the claude failure records.

title: A Refine answer built on an intent that has since expired re-installs that intent over the fallback and starts a new 45 s commitment
description: In Refine mode, ClaudeStrategist builds its answer from `context.ActiveIntent`, the intent that was active when the request was sent (Refined(active, proposed) keeps that intent's playbook, posture, objectives and budget). Nothing checks, when the answer arrives, that this intent is still the active one. The scheduler checks only age (15 s) and events of severity 0.7 or higher. The validator checks the current context but not which intent the refinement was based on. Suppose intent A expires while a fast Refine request for A is in flight. Arbiter.Update ends A and the fallback installs B. The Refine answer then arrives within 15 s and the arbiter treats it as a Primary proposal against a Fallback placeholder, reason 'yield'. So the fast model (Haiku, meant only to re-parameterise the active intent) switches the playbook back to the expired A, and ActiveSince restarts, which begins a new 45 s commitment window. For that window the slow strategist's next choice is refused with reason 'commitment'. The request's own pendingTrigger 'replan:expired' may also be routed to fast again by TwoSpeedStrategist, because ActiveIntent is non-null and lastSlow is recent.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a scratch xUnit test on a git-archive copy of HEAD, using the real StrategyScheduler, IntentArbiter, IntentValidator and TwoSpeedStrategist, cadence 5 s. The fast side mimics Refined() by keeping the request-time active playbook and posture. Slow LLM installs A (allied-boom, expires at t=28). Fast refines at t=5..20 return null, and the slow call at t=20 fails. A fast request is sent at t=25 with ActiveIntent=A. At t=28 A expires and the fallback installs fb-420 (generic-defend, role Fallback). At t=30 the Refine answer lands. Result: 'at 29 active=fb-420 role=Fallback', then 'at 30 active=refineA playbook=allied-boom role=Primary since=30'. The expired playbook is back, committed as Primary from t=30.
suggested_fix: Make a Refine proposal carry the id of the intent it refines (for example a BasedOnIntentId or ParentIntentId, or put it in the request) and discard it as late when the arbiter's Active.IntentId differs at arrival. Alternatively, have the scheduler reject a fast-path proposal whose request-time ActiveIntent is no longer arbiter.Active. Add a scheduler test for the expiry-during-Refine case.

title: Refine (Haiku) renewals turn a fallback plan into a committed one and set the incumbent confidence, so the slow Claude model is locked out
description: Refined() copies everything from the active intent except parameters, expiry, confidence, assumptions and rationale. The result always has the active intent's playbook and posture, so the arbiter treats it as a Renewal. Renew() promotes ActiveRole to Primary ('a primary strategist endorsing a placeholder's plan makes it a real commitment'), but ActiveSince stays where it was, and the incumbent Confidence becomes whatever Haiku wrote. Refine mode is meant to 'tune parameters and nothing else'. In practice it (a) removes the fallback/emergency placeholder status that lets the slow strategic model take over at once, and (b) controls the posture-hysteresis baseline. On the llm+fast arm Refine runs every 5 s against a 20 s slow cadence, so Refine usually answers before the slow model gets a turn.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary xunit probe (since deleted). Selector-fallback intent allied-boom/Boom (conf 0.6) activated with role Fallback at t=0. A Refine ClaudeStrategist whose reply has confidence 0.95 returns allied-boom/Boom, and Offer gives Renewed with role=Primary. The slow Claude proposes allied-turtle/Turtle (conf 0.9) at t=10: Refused 'commitment'. Without the refine it would have been Activated 'yield'. At t=100 the slow model proposes Turtle at confidence 1.0: Refused 'hysteresis', because 1.0-0.95 < 0.15. While Refine keeps renewing with confidence >= 0.86, the slow model can never change posture except through an abort or a base-threat override.
suggested_fix: In Refine mode keep the active intent's Confidence, and do not let a Refine renewal promote a Fallback/Emergency role to Primary. Either offer refine proposals under a distinct role or keep ActiveRole in Renew when the proposal came from the refine strategist. Alternatively, have TwoSpeedStrategist route to the slow model whenever the active intent is a placeholder.
verification:
- `src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot.Claude/ClaudeStrategist.cs:248-260`: refine rejects a playbook switch, then applies `intent = Refined(active, intent)`.
- `ClaudeStrategist.cs:275-287`: `Refined` returns `active with { ..., Confidence = proposed.Confidence, ... }`.
- `src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Arbitration/IntentArbiter.cs` `Decide`: same PlaybookId and Posture returns `Renewed "renewal"`. The check `placeholder = ActiveRole == Emergency || (ActiveRole == Fallback && role == Primary)` returns "yield". Otherwise the checks are, in order, commitment (`now.SecondsSince(ActiveSince) < MinCommit`) and then hysteresis (`challenger.Confidence - incumbent.Confidence < PostureConfidenceMargin`).

title: Replies served by the server-side fallback model cost $0 and relabel the arm's model; the declined attempt's tokens are dropped
description: Strategic requests use fallbacks:"default" (server-side-fallback-2026-07-01). On a policy decline the API re-serves the request on Anthropic's chosen fallback model, e.g. claude-opus-4-8 for cyber-category declines, and the top-level message.model names that model. ClaudeStrategist records ProposalCost.Model = reply.ModelId. PriceTable has no entry for claude-opus-4-8, and BotArenaAgent adds `PriceTable.CostUsd(...) ?? 0`, so the proposal is priced at $0. BotArenaAgent also sets `Stats.Model ??= model`, so if the first proposal was fallback-served the whole arm is reported as claude-opus-4-8. In addition, the API reports only the final attempt in top-level usage; the per-attempt breakdown is in usage.iterations, which AnthropicMessageClient ignores (lines 97/146). A mid-output decline on Opus 5 is billed at normal rates but never counted.
failure_scenario: The llm arm on a live key: one strategic request trips a classifier and the default fallback serves it from claude-opus-4-8. The reply's ModelId is 'claude-opus-4-8', PriceTable.TryGet fails and CostUsd returns null. The arena adds 0 USD for that proposal and leaves out the declined Opus 5 attempt's billed tokens. The report under-states inference cost and can name the wrong model for the arm.
suggested_fix: Price by the requested model or add every supported fallback target (claude-opus-4-8 at $5/$25) to PriceTable. Sum usage.iterations in AnthropicMessageClient (add a per-attempt list or totals to ModelReply). Make an unknown model in the arena a hard error or a flagged 'unpriced' count instead of `?? 0`. Record served-by separately from the configured model.

title: Prompt hides the arbiter's numeric acceptance rules: posture margin 0.15, base-threat ratio 1.5, and that renewal requires the same posture
description: The system prompt says only 'Changing posture needs clearly higher confidence than the incumbent's' and 'the base is under serious threat'. The arbiter refuses a posture change unless challenger.Confidence - incumbent.Confidence >= 0.15 (PostureConfidenceMargin). It overrides commitment only when BaseThreatRatio > 1.5. It counts a proposal as a renewal only when both playbook AND posture match the incumbent. The prompt tells the model to 'propose the same playbook with adjusted parameters' inside the commitment window, but does not say the posture must also be unchanged. A same-playbook proposal with a different posture is refused as 'commitment'. None of these numbers appear anywhere in the prompt, so the model cannot tell whether a proposal will be accepted.
failure_scenario: The incumbent is the model's own intent at confidence 0.8. The model decides to shift from Boom to Pressure and, following 'clearly higher', answers with confidence 0.9. The arbiter refuses it as 'hysteresis' (0.10 < 0.15), and each later cadence repeats the refused proposal. Another case: inside the commit window the model keeps the playbook but changes posture as advised, and the arbiter refuses it as 'commitment' instead of renewing it.
suggested_fix: Render the arbiter options (PostureConfidenceMargin, BaseThreatOverrideRatio, the renewal rule 'same playbookId and same posture') into the match context from the same IntentArbiterOptions the runtime uses, and state them exactly in the system prompt.

title: Intent history in the prompt fills up with renewals, so the model cannot see its earlier plan switches
description: IntentArbiter.Renew closes the previous entry with endReason 'renewed' and adds a new IntentHistoryEntry on every renewal. The prompt includes only the last historyLimit (8) entries. With a 10-30 s strategic cadence, and a 5 s cadence on llm+fast, almost every proposal is a renewal. Within 40 s to 4 min the window holds only renewals of the current playbook, and the real switches, aborts and yields drop out. The prompt tells the model that 'frequent switching loses games', but the model no longer has the history it needs to judge that.
failure_scenario: On llm+fast, the active plan allied-boom is renewed by Refine every 5 s. After 40 s the history block has 8 entries of allied-boom 'renewed'. The earlier allied-pressure intent that was aborted a minute ago, the evidence against re-trying it, is gone. The model proposes allied-pressure again and the bot oscillates.
suggested_fix: Collapse consecutive renewals of the same playbook and posture into one history item (first acceptedAt, renewal count, last end), or filter out 'renewed' endings before applying historyLimit.
